newsitem.title: USA: US stocks end sharply lower, rally attempt crushed.
newsitem.headline: US stocks end sharply lower, rally attempt crushed.

text.p: U.S. stocks ended sharply lower on Wednesday after an attempt to extend a one-day rally was quashed.
Market players said investors were unwilling to return to the market amid fears that rising interest rates would lead to further losses in the days ahead.
"Everybody has their horns pulled in," said Arnie Owen, director of equities at Kaufman Brothers.
The Dow industrials finished down 94 points, or 1.4 percent, at 6517.
The day's losses came after the Dow rebounded 28 points Tuesday on the heels of a two-session selloff that clipped almost 300 points off the closely-watched average of 30 blue chips.
With Wednesday's downturn, the Dow has fallen eight percent from its closing peak of 7085 set March 11.
Big Board losers outnumbered gainers by a 17-to-eight ratio.
The Nasdaq composite, studded with high-growth technology companies, fell 16 points to 1201, a 1.3 percent drop. The Nasdaq index has shed 13.5 percent since its January 22 peak close at 1388.

The market's malaise spread last week after the Federal Reserve moved to boost short-term interest rates for the first time in two years. The possibility of further Fed rate increases has led to concerns on Wall Street that a slowing economy will bring a slowdown in corporate profit growth.
The subsequent rise in yields on the 30-year Treasury bond over the key seven percent level has led investors to view bonds as increasingly attractive relative to volatile stocks.
On Wednesday, the long bond was up 1/32 to yield 7.07 percent in late trading. Analysts said the March employment report due Friday will be critical for bonds and stocks.
Some traders see the quarterly earnings season, which gets under way next week, as something that may stem the sell-off.

But Peggy Farley, chief executive officer at Amas Securities, said a robust dollar probably meant that few multinational corporations would post stronger-than-expected profits. "It's not over yet by any means," she said, referring to the slide in share prices.
Craig Callahan, chief investment officer at Meridian Investment Management, said his firm shifted its portfolio recommendation to about 65 percent cash for U.S. accounts more than a month ago.
Callahan said the firm raised the cash component because of the lofty valuations in stocks. "Nothing has happened in the last few days to change that," he said.
In view of the Fed rate increase, the Dow would need to drop another five to seven percent before stocks became attractively valued, barring further rate rises, he said..

Energy companies, including oil drilling and services concerns, were among the hardest hit on Wednesday as crude oil prices dropped. Schlumberger Ltd sank 3-3/8 to 106-5/8, Falcon Drilling Co Inc shed 1-5/8 to 34-1/2 and Diamond Offshore Drilling Inc eased 2-1/8 to 65-3/8.

H&R Block Inc, which owns about 80 percent of online service provider CompuServe Corp, said the two companies are in discussions with a third party regarding a possible business combination involving CompuServe.

The statement came amid market talk that industry leader American Online Inc was in talks to buy its rival. CompuServe finished up 1-5/8 to 12-5/8. American Online fell 1-1/8 to 44-5/8 and H&R Block was unchanged at 30-5/8.
Software maker FileNet Corp tumbled 4-7/8 to 11 after saying it would report a loss in its first quarter because of weak orders in U.S. and international markets.

Shares of retail pharmacy chain ShopKo Stores Inc rose 1-1/4 to 16-1/2 amid expectations that its major shareholder would find a deal to replace its canceled merger with Phar-Mor Inc. The companies called off their planned union because of "continuing uncertainties." Phar-Mor rose 3/8 to 5-3/8.
Project Software & Development Inc sank 15-15/16 to 15-5/16 after the company said its second-quarter earnings would fall short of profits in the year-earlier period.
The S&P 500 index fell 9.53 points to 750.11.
The Nasdaq Composite fell 15.93 points to 1201.00.
((-- Wall Street desk, 212-859-1730))
